page.layout: One column of running text. Small marginal fragments run down the right margin, the largest near the lines "Id ægrè" and "Elei, Messenii". Running head at top centre, page number 271 at top right.

main_text.p: ptum, ut bello ex hoste capta loca à Corcyrâ usque in Ætoliam, ædificia, muri, agri Ætolis cederent: reliqua præda Romanorum esset: operam darent Romani, ut Acarnaniâ Ætoli potirentur: neutris pacisci cum Philippo, nisi alteris quoque inclusis, liceret. Bellum hoc per varios casus gestum, tractumque in annum septimum, quo consules Romæ fuêre P. Cornelius Scipio, P. Licinius Crassus, qui erat belli Punici secundi decimus quartus. Tum Romanis alio aversis, Ætoli clade forte affecti à Philippo, & jam belli diuturni pertæsi, præproperè, ne consultis quidem Romanis, quorum jam validus exercitus in procinctu erat, auspiciis P. Sempronii proconsulis Macedoniam invasurus, pacem cum Philippo fecêre.[illegible, ~3 letters]

Id ægrè latum quidem à Romanis: sed[?] paulò post ab ipsis quoque, intercedentibus maximè Epirotis belli malorum[illegible, ~4 letters] ob viciniam non expertibus, pax cum Philippo & ejus sociis inita, ac fœdus etiam percussum: adscripti fœderi à rege Prusias Bithynus, Achæi, Bœoti, Thessali, Acarnanes, Epirotæ, quorum erat ope in bello rex usus, à Romanis Ilienses, Attalus rex, Pleuratus Illyrius; Nabis Lacedæmoniorum tyrannus,[illegible, ~2 letters] Elei, Messenii, Athenienses, quos cum[illegible, ~3 letters] Ætolis

page.notes: Right margin fragments are too faint to read and are marked as illegible. "fec" after "sed" is uncertain; the scan may show a misprint or a damaged word. The paragraph break before "Id ægrè" is not clear from the scan, so I kept it as one paragraph. The final word "Ætolis" stands at the foot as a catchword and may be part of the text.
